featured.suggestedTitle: Rust 1.95.0 Released: New Features and Improvements
featured.suggestedSummary: Rust 1.95.0 introduces significant language updates, including the stabilization of 'if let' guards on match arms and changes to the irrefutable_let_patterns lint. These enhancements improve code readability and safety by allowing more concise and expressive pattern matching. Developers can leverage these new features to write cleaner and more efficient Rust code, enhancing both performance and maintainability of Rust projects.

featured.title: Request: Provide an official way to *deprecate* a crate. NOT yank. Yank is stupid
featured.summary:
Agreed. The current situation is not great.
As a maintainer, I don't want users of my libraries to run into old bugs I've already fixed. It wastes their time, and mine too if they complain about it to me.
Even if old versions technically work fine, there's an ecosystem-wide cost of code bloat caused by multiple semver major versions being used at the same time.
So I'd like to nudge users more to upgrade, at least move off super old versions. I'm currently using yank for this, but it's too…
featured.suggestedTitle: Proposal for Official Crate Deprecation Method
featured.suggestedSummary: The Rust community is discussing a proposal to introduce an official way to deprecate crates, as opposed to the current 'yank' method. This change aims to provide a clearer and less disruptive path for managing outdated or unmaintained crates. By integrating with the RustSec database, this approach could improve ecosystem health and provide developers with better guidance on crate usage, ultimately enhancing project stability and security.
